Treatment Summary
The patient presented following a low-speed collision in a parking lot with complaints
of headache, dizziness, and cognitive fatigue consistent with concussion. The
mechanism of injury and the force of the impact are considered well matched to the
reported symptoms. Over the course of 21 visits, care included neurological
assessment, vestibular and balance evaluation, graded symptom monitoring, and
graduated return-to-activity guidance. Several examination findings, including mild
balance deficits and reduced tolerance to visual tracking tasks, support the
diagnosis, while other standard neurological tests, such as cranial nerve function,
strength, and reflexes, returned normal. No piror injury to the head or neck region is
known. Treatment followed an expected clinical course, with visit frequency and
itnensity tapering as symptoms improved and function returned. Billing records reflect
single, appropriate charges for each service rendered without duplication. Ongoing
follow-up is recommended only if symptoms recur.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.
